story: What if Paradise had cut fuel breaks before November 8, 2018?
crawl: A transmission line fails above the Feather River canyon.
Winds are 50 miles per hour, out of the northeast.
Paradise is 17 kilometers downwind. 26,000 people. 11,000 homes.
No fuel breaks stand between the fire and the town.

data.buildings: proxy: developed-land cells scaled to pre-fire home count

simplifications: Homes are estimated from developed-land cells at 2018 density, not individual footprints.
Fire spread is a calibrated graph travel-time model (Dijkstra), not fire physics - one free speed parameter fit to the historical outcome.
One uniform historical wind (35 mph from 45 degrees) for all 12 hours; no ember spotting, no weather change.
Fuel breaks slow fire 20x rather than stopping it; costs are rough mechanical-treatment magnitudes, not bids.
Fuels are LANDFIRE LF2016_FBFM40 (LF 2016 Remap, pre-fire), terrain LANDFIRE LF2020_Elev, both resampled to a 60 m grid.
